name: Amos Tate
life: “I still remember wrapping my first frozen order in a football shirt.” Sunday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Amos often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I lost a day's ice. I want the contractor to pay the stallholders who lost sales too.
appearance: Amos has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for close-cropped dark curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Amos raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Amos carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To recover the stallholders' lost ice sales.
family: Harriet Sloan is Amos’s half-sibling. Amos chooses whether to use it. Harriet saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The aquarium*, Harriet says, “I wrote abandoned on the inventory because the flat was empty.”
connections: Remy Monroe. A lost ice sale and a morning spent translating become two claims on the same contractor.

reactions.response: Amos checks with the intended recipient before leaving a late parcel.
